subject: Penetration pack request for Private VPC deployment - artifacts & scope
messages:
From: Elena Morales <security@finedge.com>
To: maya.srinivasan@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Request: pen test artifacts for our Private VPC deployment

Hi Maya,

Following up from our procurement security review: before we can finalize the private deployment engagement, FinEdge needs a complete set of penetration-testing artifacts specific to the Redwood instance that will run in our AWS account. Specifically we need:

- Full pen-test report (pdf) from the external assessor covering network + host findings for the deployment boundary you expect us to use.
- Raw findings/CSV (raw identifiers, CVE refs) and associated severity mapping.
- A list of external IPs and domains used by the tester during the engagement (allowlist).
- Evidence of remediation and timestamps (patch notes, logs, or retest notes) for any high/critical findings.
- Network boundary diagram and a short write-up of the boundary assumptions for a Private/VPC deployment (eg which components live in customer VPC vs Redwood-managed infra).
- Proposed retest schedule and whether a follow-up assessment was performed.

We also need to understand whether any tenant-level identifiers or customer-specific secrets are included in the pack so we can redline before uploading to our evidence repository.

Please let me know if you can share these artifacts, and whether you need an NDA or any redaction before we accept. Our security review is targeting an approval decision by 2026-09-15.

Thanks,
Elena Morales
Head of Security, FinEdge Bank
elena.morales@finedge.com

Attachment: procurement-questionnaire-FinEdge-20260828.pdf (pdf)

From: Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <security@finedge.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, alex_martinez@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 10:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: pen test artifacts for our Private VPC deployment

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. We can provide a penetration pack that contains:

- executive-friendly pen test report (pdf)
- raw findings CSV (sanitized as needed)
- IP/domain list used by the assessor
- network boundary diagram and assumptions document
- remediation evidence (patch records / logs)

Neha will review for any tenant-specific identifiers that need redaction. Marcus is pulling the latest pack from our assessor (AstraSec) and will confirm which files we can share directly vs. which require redaction or a redline.

Proposed timeline: we can get a sanitized penetration pack to you by 2026-09-05 and schedule a short call to review the remediation evidence the week of 2026-09-07. If FinEdge requires a signed NDA for the raw CSV, we will accommodate — please send the NDA link if preferred.

Thanks,
Maya Srinivasan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
maya.srinivasan@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Cc: alex_martinez@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: AstraSec pack pulled — contents and lift notes

Maya / Neha — I pulled the latest pack from AstraSec. Summary of contents and items for redaction:

Included in penetration-pack-astrasec-20260901.zip:
- full_report_astrasec_redwood_private_vpc.pdf (executive + technical findings)
- findings_raw_20260901.csv (hostnames/IPs, CVE refs, reproduction steps)
- ip_allowlist_tested.txt (IP ranges and ephemeral jump host IPs)
- poc_videos/ (screenshots + short clips for highest severity items)
- timeline_and_scope.txt (dates, test windows, test team contact)

Also attaching: redwood_vpc_boundary_diagram_v2.pdf (diagram showing which components execute in customer VPC vs Redwood-managed remote control plane) and patch-trace-logs.csv (evidence exported from our patch management system showing applied fixes and timestamps).

What I recommend for sharing with FinEdge:
- Share full_report_astrasec_redwood_private_vpc.pdf (no redaction).
- Share ip_allowlist_tested.txt and timeline_and_scope.txt as-is.
- Sanitize findings_raw_20260901.csv to remove internal hostnames and any tenant IDs — replace with generic placeholders (HOST-###).
- Exclude poc_videos/ from the initial share until we get written approval from FinEdge security (videos may contain internal screenshots with identifiable tenant metadata).

Status of high/critical items:
- Two medium findings (improper config on ephemeral admin endpoint) — fixed 2026-08-25, patch-ids in patch-trace-logs.csv.
- One low severity info-leak — accepted as low risk by engineering; mitigation scheduled for 2026-09-10.

Please confirm if I should proceed with the redaction and prepare the sanitized CSV for 2026-09-05 delivery.

Attachments: redwood_vpc_boundary_diagram_v2.pdf, penetration-pack-astrasec-20260901.zip, patch-trace-logs.csv

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Security Operations Lead, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com, maya.srinivasan@redwood.com
Cc: alex_martinez@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 11:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: AstraSec pack pulled — contents and lift notes

Marcus — good summary. A couple of gating items before we share the sanitized pack with FinEdge:

1) Redaction rules: remove any customer-specific tenant IDs, internal traceroute IDs, and full internal hostnames. Replace hostnames with HOST-000 style placeholders and ensure reproduction steps don't include screenshots with embedded identifiers.
2) Logs: patch-trace-logs.csv is OK to share but we should remove any internal ticket IDs that reference our private backlog (Jira keys). Timestamps and patch IDs are fine.
3) Videos/screenshots: only share when FinEdge signs an evidence NDA (we should ask Elena to confirm).
4) IPs: ip_allowlist_tested.txt is fine to share, but blank out any ephemeral developer machines among the list (we will note those as 'ephemeral dev IPs — redacted').

If we follow the above, I'm comfortable with the sanitized pack being delivered on 2026-09-05. Also, please add a short cover note that explains our boundary assumptions: e.g., control plane endpoints are Redwood-managed in our hosted control plane; inference worker VMs and data storage live in the customer VPC; egress is via customer NAT gateways unless otherwise configured.

Neha Kapoor
Security Engineering Manager, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com

- redwood_vpc_boundary_diagram_v2.pdf: diagram + legend explaining which components run in FinEdge VPC vs Redwood-managed control plane
